body.target_estimand: \[S_{\bullet u}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)=\{(\tau_{\omega}(v\leftarrow u))_{v\in V}:\omega\in\Omega^{\star}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\},\qquad S_{vu}=\{x_v:x\in S_{\bullet u}\}.\]
body.estimand_functional: For \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), \(S_{\bullet u}=\{e_u\}\). For \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]\), \[S_{\bullet u}=\left\{W_{\bullet c}/W_{uc}:(u,c)\in P_g\right\}\cup\bigl(\{e_u\}\text{ if }z_u=1\bigr),\qquad S_{vu}=\{x_v:x\in S_{\bullet u}\}.\] Every vector is attained by one globally minimum completion, \(|S_{\bullet u}|\le q+1\), and this cap is attained for every \(q\ge1\) by an explicitly separable canonical, minimal, rank-faithful model. The full total-effect-matrix image remains indexed by \(\Omega^\star\) and need not factor through the marginals \(P_g\). On rational promised inputs, \(\mathrm{COMP\text{-}EDGE}\) is in promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\), exact optimization and search are in \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\), and fixed block interaction width \(b\) gives deterministic time \((pq)^b\operatorname{poly}(p,q,\text{input bit length})\); the unrestricted deterministic complexity remains open.

sampling_model.design: Population exact identification on the real generic domain of Yang et al.'s recovered mixing equivalence class, with exact rational encoding used only for the separate completion-complexity question.
sampling_model.units: The population layer is indexed by the observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\). An optional region-union remark may start from \(n\) i.i.d. observations, but no first-stage inferential construction is a contribution.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention fixes a labeled substantive variable \(u\), including a variable measured with error or a fixed singleton mleaf.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used because the population target is a linear structural intervention effect recovered from the mixing representation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population core takes real \(W\) as the separable identification input. Rational \(\widetilde W\) is introduced only for exact \(\operatorname{CompOpt}\) bit complexity. Construction, alignment, and computation of any confidence region for an overcomplete mixing matrix are outside scope.

comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\) theorem and bounded-block tractability theorem give upper bounds while the unrestricted complexity question remains open.

comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The no-measurement proposition proves equivalence on the shared generic subclass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 4 enumerates observationally compatible effect possibilities in latent-variable LiNGAM without simultaneous measurement error.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The complete joint-column image extends the normalized-column architecture to known measurement labels and center reassignment.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Maximum-flow rank tests identify parameters under a different general-confounding model but do not optimize mixed DOG completions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The unrestricted completion question remains informed by, but is not resolved by, those flow reductions.

comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The plateau certificate and open unrestricted complexity question delimit why local traversal is insufficient.

comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The exact mixed-DOG image is analogous in reporting purpose but requires globally minimum feasible pairs.

body.tldr: For Yang et al.'s canonical separable, minimal, rank-faithful linear model with latent confounding, measurement error, and known labels, the note proves the exact jointly attained intervention-column image over every minimum-edge DOG reconstruction. A fixed mleaf contributes \(e_u\); otherwise the image consists of normalized retained columns from globally feasible pairs, together with \(e_u\) when the intervention label can be an mleaf. Every vector has one attaining minimum model, the cardinality bound \(q+1\) is sharp for every \(q\ge1\) by an explicit Bernoulli-zonotope separability construction, and scalar singletonness is exactly a zero/minor comparison. Exact rational completion lies in promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\), with optimization and search in \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\); fixed per-block interaction width is deterministically tractable even with arbitrarily many ambiguous groups overall. The unrestricted deterministic complexity remains open, and projected group marginals do not factor the full total-effect-matrix image.

project_justification.gap: Yang et al.'s Theorem 3 gives a generic minimum-edge DOG class and Algorithm 2 enumerates a Cartesian family, but it does not state the complete labeled joint total-effect-column image or classify exact constrained minimum completion. Prior latent-variable LiNGAM effect criteria omit simultaneous measurement-label restrictions and center-to-mleaf reassignment. Exact downstream cancellations make local edge scores invalid.
project_justification.niche: The intervention column depends only on the selected center/noise pair in the intervention label's unique recovered group, although membership of that pair in a global minimum remains coupled across groups. This separates an exact algebraic identification theorem from a sharply localized discrete optimization problem while preserving coherent joint witnesses.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the normalized reconstruction, complete jointly attained intervention-column image, scalar and joint singleton minor criteria, a universal sharp \(q+1\) cap with an explicit separable in-class witness, a faithful twelve-edge plateau obstruction, promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\) and \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper bounds, deterministic fixed-width block tractability, the oracle-to-all-images reduction, and the no-measurement equivalence. It leaves only the unrestricted deterministic completion classification open.

body.related_work: Yang, Nafea, Kiyavash, Zhang, and Ghassami (2026), Definition 2, Theorems 2--3, Algorithms 1--2, Proposition 7, and Appendix A.4 supply the canonical model, corrected rank-faithfulness and minimality setting, recovered ancestral ordered groups, and probability-one simultaneous DOG faithfulness used here. Their Cartesian enumeration does not imply a polynomial minimum-completion algorithm. Salehkaleybar, Ghassami, Kiyavash, and Zhang (2020), Section 4, provide the closest normalized-column effect-image precedent without simultaneous measurement error. Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Drton, and Kiyavash (2024), Theorem 3.3, give the complete unknown-graph criterion in the no-measurement subclass; the reduction proposition proves agreement there rather than claiming that criterion as new. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026) use determinant ranks and nonintersecting paths for a different identification problem, and Wienoebst, Luttermann, Bannach, and Liskiewicz (2023) give linear-delay Markov-equivalence traversal; neither controls the coupled support cancellations in exact mixed-DOG completion. Maathuis, Kalisch, and Buehlmann (2009) motivate reporting possible effects without full DAG enumeration, but their local CPDAG computation does not supply globally minimum mixed-DOG pairs. The present computational contribution is therefore an exact verification/oracle envelope and a fixed-block-width algorithm, not a resolution of unrestricted complexity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The effect image needs only the projected global-minimum pairs \(P_g\), but unrestricted computation of those projections remains unclassified. The faithful benchmark has a thirteen-edge strict coordinate trap and a coupled repair attaining the twelve-edge optimum, so additive per-group costs and strict coordinate descent are invalid. The bounded-block theorem enumerates complete assignments only within blocks having at most fixed \(b\) nontrivial groups and verifies every assignment exactly; it does not assume that a singleton candidate is legal. Population observational completeness is relative-Zariski generic over real canonical coefficient strata with source-law separability separate. Rational inputs are used only for deterministic bit complexity, with no probability claim on rational points.
body.honest_scope: The structural target is the complete joint column \(\{(\tau_\omega(v\leftarrow u))_{v\in V}:\omega\in\Omega^\star\}\), and each scalar image is only its coordinate projection. Deterministic reconstruction and image equalities hold for fixed \(W\), recovered groups, known labels, and a nonempty finite global argmin. Equality with the full observationally compatible minimum-edge Yang DOG class additionally uses separability, corrected minimality and Assumption 3, and \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\); Appendix A.4's finite-class probability-one argument is used only there. The \(q+1\) joint-column cap is attained for every \(q\ge1\) by a two-row rational construction whose independent Bernoulli sources make the full mixing directions identifiable from the observed support zonotope. Exact \(\mathrm{COMP\text{-}EDGE}\) verification is polynomial, optimization/search have \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper bounds, and fixed block interaction width is polynomial for fixed \(b\). No unrestricted polynomial-time or hardness classification is claimed, and no factorization of the full total-effect-matrix image across \(P_g\) marginals is claimed. Inference remains external: a supplied simultaneous region containing \(W\) transfers coverage to the union of these exact images by event inclusion, but this core constructs neither that region nor a uniform first-stage limit theorem.
